Edge 4 already supplies a conv path to the output, so a second one adds less.
A conv on the direct input-output edge adds more when the node-2 path into the output is missing.
Without the direct edge, edge 5 is a main route to the output, so conv gains more.
Without the direct edge, edge 4 is a key route to the output.
Restoring the only input to node 1 with a conv gains more than replacing another op.
With edge 4 cut, edge 0's signal reaches the output only through edges 2 and 5, so it matters less.
A skip helps more when the output has few other paths, as it adds a gradient shortcut.
Deleting a conv on an output edge is more damaging than deleting a weak op.
Replacing a conv with pooling loses much more accuracy than replacing weaker ops.
